If you’re using “bonjour” and “ça va” just to look polished, then yes, it can become performance. A good test: are you willing to be corrected without getting defensive? If someone laughs kindly and says, “No, say it like this,” do you feel embarrassed but grateful, or do you feel your image has been damaged? Respect survives correction. Performance hates correction.

Also, not every act of respect needs to be deep or fluent. Sometimes “bonjour,” “ça va,” “merci,” said warmly and consistently, is enough to show that you’re present. The point isn’t to become a perfect speaker overnight. The point is to make the other person feel they are not invisible.

So I’d call it respect if it stays humble, repeated, and connected to real listening. Big respect for trying small things properly. That’s not empty pageantry; that’s bridge-building, sha.
